goals: Quantify how water partitioning (ET, runoff, recharge) differs between a wet year (1993) and a dry year (2002) across the Salt River headwaters' elevation gradient
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (900-3300 m, controls precip amount/phase via NLDAS-2)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column runs stratified by elevation, each run under both wet (1993) and dry (2002) forcing, to isolate the temporal forcing contrast across the spatial gradient. NLDAS-2 forcing (available in CONUS) provides elevation-varying precipitation/temperature, enabling the elevation driver to act through climate.

answerable: Wet vs dry partitioning contrast (ET, runoff, recharge) across elevation — NLDAS-2 forcing is available in-domain and provides elevation-varying precip/temp
Modeled snow/SWE output (H2OSNO) — can report, though validation is limited by sparse SNOTEL

not_answerable.aspect: Co-located streamflow validation at USGS gauges
not_answerable.why: ELM columns are independent 1-D points with no lateral routing — cannot aggregate column runoff over contributing areas to compare against integrated gage discharge
SNOTEL observations are sparse in-domain (per brief's observations_missing)
not_answerable.needs: Denser SNOTEL coverage or alternative snow observation dataset

sampling_strategy.approach: Stratified by elevation (3 bands spanning 900-3300 m) × forcing period (2 treatments: wet 1993, dry 2002). Each spatial column is run under both forcing years, creating a 2-treatment factorial design.

bands: Low (900-1600 m): rain-dominated, lower orographic precip
Mid (1600-2400 m): rain-snow transition, peak orographic precip

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 replicates per band = 6 unique spatial locations. Each location is run under both 1993 and 2002 forcing (12 column-years total). Light replication (2 per band) captures within-band soil/aspect variability while keeping N small. The 3 bands resolve the rain-snow transition and orographic gradient, which are the key mechanisms for partitioning sensitivity to wet vs dry forcing.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in mid-elevation (1600-2400 m) rain-snow transition where partitioning sensitivity is highest. Within each band, prefer valley bottoms / riparian corridors where soil moisture and runoff generation are most active. Avoid extreme ridgetops (NLDAS 12 km cells average over terrain, may underestimate ridgetop precip).
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 columns per elevation band to capture within-band heterogeneity (soil, aspect) without excessive cost.

sampling_plan.reason: Isolate low-elevation rain-dominated partitioning response to wet vs dry forcing (minimal snow influence).
Capture rain-snow transition zone where partitioning is most sensitive to forcing (snowmelt timing shifts between wet/dry years).
Isolate high-elevation snow-dominated response where snowpack accumulation/melt timing differ strongly between wet/dry years.

validation_design.comparison: analog — compare modeled runoff TIMING (peak month, recession shape) from columns in the gage's elevation band against observed hydrograph timing. NOT co-located magnitude (requires routing to aggregate column runoff over contributing area).
validation_design.metric: Peak-month agreement, timing correlation (not magnitude/bias — routing needed for that)
validation_design.n_validation_points: 1-2 gauges (depends on gage density in HUC 15060103)

validation_design.comparison: Co-located (if SNOTEL sites exist) — compare modeled H2OSNO peak against observed peak SWE. Sparse coverage limits robustness.
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — SNOTEL is sparse per brief

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: Each of 6 spatial columns run under both 1993 (wet) and 2002 (dry) NLDAS-2 forcing. WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013 equilibrium WTD) for initial aquifer state. Native SSURGO soil at each location. One-year runs (no multi-year spin-up needed with WTD initialization).

requires_capabilities.why: To sum per-column runoff over contributing areas and validate against USGS gage integrated discharge
requires_capabilities.blocks: Co-located streamflow magnitude validation (timing-only analog validation is possible without routing)

requires_capabilities.why: To initialize aquifer storage / water table at equilibrium without multi-year spin-up cost (preferred for 1-year forcing comparisons)
requires_capabilities.blocks: Nothing — this capability is AVAILABLE per guidance (preferred over multi-year spin-up). Listed here as a dependency to confirm its use.

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL data ingest / denser snow observation coverage
requires_capabilities.why: To robustly validate modeled peak SWE (current coverage is sparse per brief)
requires_capabilities.blocks: Robust peak-SWE validation (modeled snow output is available, but validation is limited)

assumptions: NLDAS-2 forcing is available and adequate for the Salt River headwaters (verified: within CONUS domain, 0.125° resolution provides ~15 distinct precip values across 2400 m relief)
1993 and 2002 are representative wet and dry years (user-specified)
Soil heterogeneity is secondary to elevation/climate effects (soil not listed as candidate driver)
One-year runs (1993, 2002) are sufficient with WTD-informed initialization (no multi-year spin-up needed)
Within-band replication (n=2) adequately captures soil/aspect variability
USGS gage density in HUC 15060103 supports 1-2 validation points (actual count unknown)
open_questions: What is the actual USGS gage density in HUC 15060103 (how many gauges, where)?
Are there any SNOTEL sites within or near the domain (even if sparse)?
Should we add a 'normal' year (e.g. median precip year) as a third forcing treatment for context?
Is soil heterogeneity significant enough to warrant stratification (not listed as candidate driver, but may matter)?
